items.title: Two sides must enclose the angle
items.student: Draw a triangle with sides8cm and10cm enclosing30°. Drop a perpendicular to show why its area is(1/2)ab sinC. Compute area. Explain why using a30°angle elsewhere without checking which sides enclose it would be invalid. Compare with side pair6cm,9cm, included60°;round final area to2decimalplaces.

items.title: Measure a real paper triangle
items.student: On clean blank paper construct triangle with two legs from a common vertex of approximately8cm and10cm enclosing approximately30°using ruler/protractor;teacher may supply a safe triangle cut-out instead. Each learner measures both chosen sides and their included acute angle,records instrument/resolution,and computes a measured area with the sine rule. Independently measure a perpendicular height for a base-height comparison. Do not replace actual readings with the ideal design values.

items.title: Heron uses three valid sides
items.student: For a triangle with sides13,14,15cm,find semiperimeter s=(a+b+c)/2and A=sqrt[s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)]. State every substitution and units. Repeat for3,4,5cm,and check the latter by a right-triangle base-height method. Explain why perimeter and semiperimeter differ.

items.title: Check feasibility before a square root
items.student: Test side sets2,3,6cm and2,3,5cm:can each form a nondegenerate triangle? For a safe paper triangle each learner measures all three sides and computes Heron area with the actual values;compare with a base-height check if possible. Do not ignore a negative/zero radicand or force a physical result.

items.title: Parallelogram:sloping side is not height
items.student: A parallelogram has adjacent sides8cm and5cm with included acute angle30°. Draw and compute perpendicular height to the8cmbase and area. Compare with another parallelogram of the same sides but60°included angle. Explain why a constant perimeter does not force constant area.
items.teacher: Height5sin30=2.5cm,area8*5sin30=20cm². At60area20sqrt3≈34.64cm²,height5sqrt3/2≈4.33cm. Sameperimeter26cm,differentheight/area. A=bh=ab sinθ;do notuse8*5unlessincluded90°. No obtuseangleextensionrequired.

items.title: Rhombus:two compatible area routes
items.student: A rhombus has side6cm and included acute angle30°. Compute area withs²sinθ. Separately a rhombus has perpendicular diagonals10cm and8cm;compute area using half their product and explain the perpendicular-triangle partition. Can you assume those diagonal lengths belong to the first rhombus?

items.title: Regular pentagon:from side to apothem
items.student: Use the supplied regular-pentagon schematic,not a scale measurement. Join centre to vertices and side midpoints. Explain central angle360/5=72°and half-angle36°. For side4cm,derive apothem a=(s/2)/tan36°and area(1/2)(5s)a. Round final area to2decimalplaces. Explain which equal-angle/side assumptions depend on regularity.

items.title: Regular hexagon splits into six equilateral triangles
items.student: Use supplied regular-hexagon schematic. Explain central angle60°and why centre-to-vertex radius equals side s. For side4cm,compute area6*(1/2)s²sin60°and compare with(1/2)perimeter×apothem,whereapothem=s cos30°. Explain why a six-sided figure alone is not enough.

items.title: A measured classroom design application
items.student: Choose teacher-approved regular pentagon/hexagon paper templates or safe flat patterns;check approximate equal sides/angles before using regular formulas. Each learner measures side length and records tool/precision;estimate area and,wherepossible,check measured apothem. For a separate exact fictional regular-hexagon tile side10cm,find one tile area;ten nonoverlapping whole tiles cover how much area ignoring gaps? Explain why dividing a room area by tile area alone does not prove an exact tiling or purchasing count.

items.title: Audit the area claims
items.student: Correct:(1)Heron uses the full perimeter as s;(2)parallelogram area is always product of adjacent side lengths;(3)any five-sided shape with equal sides has the regular-pentagon area formula;(4)twice the length scale gives twice the area. Justify with a formula/model and give one useful practical area application with a limitation.
